chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Mubārak, the غلام of Shuʿayb, who said:
I heard Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:

I did not enrich the rich due to an honor of his before Me, and I did not impoverish the poor due to a humiliation of his before Me. Rather, it is among that by which I test the rich through the poor, and were it not for the poor, the rich would not deserve Paradise.

key_terms.ابْتَلَيْتُ: I tested; indicating divine trial and examination
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise; the hereafter reward merited through obedience and righteousness
key_terms.الْغَنِيَّ: the wealthy person; one granted material abundance
key_terms.الْفَقِيرَ: the poor person; one lacking material means
key_terms.لِكَرَامَةٍ: because of honor; meaning special esteem or rank
key_terms.لِهَوَانٍ: because of humiliation; meaning lowliness or disgrace

ai.seo_question: Does wealth mean honor with Allah and poverty mean disgrace?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that wealth and poverty are not, in themselves, signs of a person's honor or humiliation before Allah. Rather, they are part of divine trial, and the wealthy are tested through their conduct toward the poor; through fulfilling their duties toward them, they may merit Paradise.
